items.title: [@angular/router] @angular/router: Denial of Service via Unmatched Empty-Path Outlet Route Matching in Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
items.summary: A denial of service (DoS) vulnerability was identified in @angular/router when Server-Side Rendering (SSR) is enabled on Node.js (V8).During route recognition, @angular/router fails to validate whether an auxiliary outlet segment in the URL matches a route configured for that specific outlet name. Because unconfigured empty-path outlet groups (such as a:/(), x:/(...), or ///(...)) are not rejected during matching, the router repeatedly re-evaluates the route configuration against each arbitrary outlet segment provided in the URL.When a request URL contains multiple arbitrary empty-path outlet segments, this improper matching forces the router to instantiate duplicate ActivatedRouteSnapshot trees, repeatedly execute canMatch guards and route resolvers, and allocate separate copies of route parameters and queryParams for each unconfigured outlet.An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this behavior by sending requests with crafted outlet segments to exhaust the Node.js memory heap or overwhelm CPU resources, leading to SSR worker termination and service disruption.ImpactSuccessful exploitation allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust the Node.js heap with a single crafted request or a small number of concurrent requests, terminating the SSR worker process with a fatal JavaScript heap out-of-memory crash. When the matched routes declare canMatch guards or resolvers, a single short request can also trigger repeated guard or resolver executions, increasing load on backend services and holding worker connections open.Transient Allocation: Memory is released once route recognition completes; there is no persistent memory leak. The primary impact is process termination.Client-side SPAs Unaffected: Client-side Angular applications running in the browser are not vulnerable, as browser memory consumption does not cross a security boundary.Prerendering (SSG) Unaffected: Build-time prerendering does not process attacker-supplied request URLs.Attack Preconditions & Vulnerable ConfigurationsAn application is affected only if all of the following conditions are met:SSR Enabled: The application renders on demand on a Node.js / V8 server.Susceptible Route Configuration: At least one level of the route configuration contains either:an empty-path (path: "") route (e.g., {path: "", component: ShopPage}), ora route assigned to a named outlet (e.g., {path: "dashboard", children: [{path: ":id", outlet: "detail", component: DetailPanel}]}).Upstream Request Line Forwarding: Request lines reach the Node.js process without being rejected upstream by edge proxies. Node.js accepts request headers up to 16 KiB by default. Guard/resolver amplification requires only a short URL.Constrained Heap Size: Worker heaps are sized small enough relative to the request payload and concurrency (e.g., containers or serverless instances configured with 128 MiB–1 GiB).Exploit Payload ExamplesAgainst a configuration with empty-path (path: "") routes and query parameters:GET /shop/(a:/()//b:/()//c:/()//...)?param1=value&param2=value... HTTP/1.1Host: example.comAgainst a configuration with named-outlet or sibling routes:GET /dashboard/(detail:1//x:/(detail:1//x:/(...)//y:/(...))//y:/(...)) HTTP/1.1Host: example.comPatchesThe issue is resolved in angular/angular#71055. The router now requires every child outlet segment group to match a route configured for its target outlet before unwrapping child segments or completing a match, and prevents unconfigured empty-path outlet groups from matching routes declared for other outlets.Patched versions:22.2.121.2.2520.3.33Versions prior to v20 are also affected but are no longer supported and will not receive a patch.Workarounds & MitigationsIf you cannot immediately upgrade to a patched version, apply one or more of the following mitigations:Reject Parenthesized or Empty-Path Outlet URLs in Middleware or WAF (Recommended):In @angular/router, auxiliary outlet groups in a URL always use parentheses (...), and empty-path outlet groups in a URL always take the form :/( , (/ , or ///( .If your application does not use named (auxiliary) outlets in URLs, reject requests whose path contains ( or ) before Angular SSR handles the request.If your application does use named outlets, reject requests whose path contains empty-path outlet sequences (:/( , (/ , or ///( ).Unlike URL length limits, this completely blocks both heap exhaustion and short-URL guard/resolver amplification:// server.ts (placed before Angular SSR handler)app.use((req, res, next) => {  let pathname: string;  try {    pathname = decodeURI(req.url.split(/[?#]/, 1)[0]);  } catch {    res.status(400).send("Bad Request");    return;  }  // Option A: If the app does not use named outlets in URLs, block all parenthesized groups:  if (/[()]/.test(pathname)) {    res.status(400).send("Bad Request");    return;  }  // Option B: If the app uses named outlets, block only empty-path outlet groups:  if (/:\/\(|\(\//\(|\/\/\/\(/.test(pathname)) {    res.

items.title: [hono] Hono: `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths
items.summary: SummaryserveStatic decodes the request path a second time after Hono has already decoded it for routing. A crafted request can be routed as one path and served as another, so middleware mounted on a static prefix does not run for a file under that prefix.DetailsHono decodes the request path once before routing. serveStatic decoded it again before resolving the file. With a malformed percent-encoded sequence, the first decode leaves part of the path encoded, the router matches the encoded form, and the second decode resolves the real directory. The file is still resolved inside the configured root; this is not a traversal outside it.ImpactAn unauthenticated attacker may reach static files without the middleware on their prefix running, for example an authentication check. This affects applications that mount middleware on part of the directory served by serveStatic. Applications that serve only public files are not affected.Referenceshttps://github.com/honojs/hono/security/advisories/GHSA-5r4p-p66f-jhc7https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111757https://github.com/honojs/hono/commit/8b05c774ef1555c70f5ba5e2991b7e77cc3635cchttps://github.com/honojs/hono/releases/tag/v4.13.11https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5r4p-p66f-jhc7

items.title: [@angular/platform-server] @angular/platform-server: Open Redirect via Protocol-Relative URLs in Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
items.summary: An open redirect vulnerability was identified in @angular/platform-server when Server-Side Rendering (SSR) is enabled.When Angular SSR renders an incoming request, URL resolution and platform navigation are managed by ServerPlatformLocation using resolveUrl (or parseUrl in v20). While resolveUrl rejected protocol-relative URLs whose raw string directly started with //, this check ran prior to WHATWG URL normalization.When a request URL includes a popping dot-segment followed by multiple slashes (such as /.//evil.test or serialized from router route shapes like /.;/(//evil.test)), the input bypassed the initial urlStr.startsWith('//') check. Subsequent WHATWG URL parsing resolved the dot-segments and resulted in a pathname starting with // (//evil.test).Consequently, ServerPlatformLocation stored pathname = '//evil.test'. When @angular/ssr detected a mismatch between the rendered URL and the router's final location state, it emitted the unnormalized pathname into the HTTP Location response header, producing an HTTP 302 redirect with Location: //evil.test, which browsers resolve as a protocol-relative navigation off-origin.ImpactSuccessful exploitation allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to craft URLs that trick Angular SSR into redirecting users to an arbitrary external domain.Bypasses Application-Level Guards: Common application-level validation routines (such as checking !returnUrl.startsWith('//') before invoking router.navigateByUrl) accept /.//evil.test or /.;/(//evil.test) as a safe relative path, allowing attackers to bypass redirect allowlists.Client-side SPAs Unaffected: Pure client-side Angular applications (Single Page Applications without SSR) are not vulnerable, as ServerPlatformLocation is only utilized in server-side execution environments.Attack Preconditions & Vulnerable ConfigurationsAn application is affected if the following conditions are met:SSR Enabled: The application runs in a Server-Side Rendering environment using @angular/platform-server and @angular/ssr.Parameter Route Shapes: The router contains parameter routes with wildcard or child segments (e.g. /:tenant matching . and serializing secondary outlet groups (//evil.test) to /.//evil.test), or passes user-provided navigation targets (e.g. returnUrl).Reverse Proxy Passthrough: Upstream reverse proxies (Nginx, Cloudflare, ALB) pass semicolons (;) or dot-segments without stripping or normalizing them.Exploit Payload ExampleAn attacker sends a request targeting a route with parameters and child segments:GET /.;/(//evil.test) HTTP/1.1Host: example.comResponse:HTTP/1.1 302 FoundLocation: //evil.testThe client browser resolves //evil.test protocol-relatively and redirects the user away from example.com to evil.test.PatchesThe issue is resolved by updating resolveUrl (and parseUrl in v20) in @angular/platform-server to verify that the normalized URL pathname does not start with // when allowProtocolRelative is false.22.2.121.2.2520.3.33Workarounds & MitigationsIf you cannot immediately upgrade to a patched version, apply one of the following mitigations at your edge reverse proxy or WAF:Reject Paths with Dot-Segments Followed by Slashes:Configure your reverse proxy (e.g., Nginx, Cloudflare, AWS WAF) to block requests containing /.//, /..//, or /.;/:# Nginx example: reject suspicious path normalization sequencesif ($request_uri ~* "(\n/\.\/|\/\.\;)") {    return 400;}Sanitize Redirect Headers:Ensure edge proxies or API gateways rewrite or disallow protocol-relative (//) Location response headers originating from the SSR upstream.Referenceshttps://github.com/angular/angular/security/advisories/GHSA-w739-gvwx-grc3https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71077https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71078https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71079https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/450af9c813c7660b9bd91e5635f705ee3ed7b32ahttps://github.com/angular/angular/commit/83944fc8c50e86be90e8ec4184cd15002b5af262https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/928dcfd2582152655b5559509d057bf6a5a19521https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/d7d81e189d227108c3b9d39178dbb7389f6f970dhttps://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/v20.3.33https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/v21.2.25https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/v22.2.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w739-gvwx-grc3

items.title: [markdown-it] markdown-it: Quadratic complexity in smartquotes with unmatched closing quotes
items.summary: ImpactWhen typographer: true is enabled, specially crafted Markdown can cause quadratic processing time in the smartquotes rule, potentially leading to denial of service in applications processing untrusted input.Many opening double quotes followed by unmatched closing single quotes cause repeated scans of the entire opener stack. The same issue occurs with the quote types reversed.The default configuration (typographer: false) is not affected, but this option is enabled with high probability.Reproductionimport MarkdownIt from 'markdown-it'import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'const md = new MarkdownIt({ typographer: true })for (const k of [2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]) {  const input = '"a '.repeat(k) + "b' ".repeat(k)  const start = performance.now()  md.render(input)  console.log(input.length, (performance.now() - start).toFixed(1), 'ms')}Result:input sizetime1200018ms2400047ms48000115ms96000428ms1920001586msPatchesFixed in 15.0.2 and 14.3.2.WorkaroundsDisable typography with typographer: false, or disable only the smartquotes rule:md.disable('smartquotes')Referenceshttps://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/security/advisories/GHSA-r7fv-28h4-cvq7https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-111759https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/commit/1b379c1b6d0522421bd1a51b77337c79af2c8670https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/commit/cf27366035edf9196667110c47d9d67b030a4152https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/commit/daf5a3c32303e5d9de01b12eeb725fb5990b8162https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/releases/tag/14.3.2https://github.com/markdown-it/markdown-it/releases/tag/15.0.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r7fv-28h4-cvq7
